Romanian Business News - ACTMedia :: Services | About us | Contact | RSS Home Daily Financial & banking Economic Companies Energy & Environment Almost half of fraud cases reported in the first half of 2026 were phone scams (vishing) ING Bank Romania, together with the National Directorate for Cyber Security (DNSC), the Romanian Police, and the Romanian Institute for Active Aging, organized ING SAFE Talks, a new event dedicated to informing the public about the latest methods of digital fraud. For the first time, telephone scams rank first among all types of fraud. Of the total incidents reported by the DNSC in the first half of the year, 42% were telephone scams (vishing), 14% were phishing scams, and 13% were SMS scams (smishing). Nationwide, in the first half of 2026, all criminal investigation units within the Romanian Police (which have jurisdiction over the investigation of cybercrimes and crimes against computer systems) recorded approximately 15,000 criminal cases. At the end of June, approximately 72,000 cases remained pending nationwide. As of January 1, 2026, there were 67,000 cases on record, according to representatives of the Criminal Investigations Directorate of the Romanian Police. ING Bank, DNSC, and the Romanian Institute for Active Aging are calling for increased vigilance against digital fraud During the ING SAFE Talks event, participants discussed the latest digital fraud schemes, how Romanians over 50 and seniors react to fraud, and new features from the ING SAFE ecosystem dedicated to fraud prevention were launched. “The methods used by attackers aren’t necessarily new, but the technology they use has evolved significantly, including through the use of artificial intelligence tools. At the same time, they are becoming increasingly skilled at social engineering techniques, which they use to convince people to provide them with data, send them money, or install malicious applications. As users, we must continue to be vigilant about three elements that we can identify in every fraud attempt – emotion, urgency, followed by a request for data. Initiatives such as today’s, in which ING, the DNSC, the Romanian Police, civil society, and the Romanian media come together to discuss the latest scenarios and stories used in fraud attempts, are essential – prevention remains just as important as responding to cyberattacks.” – Mihai Rotariu, Manager of the Communications, Marketing, and Media Division, National Directorate for Cybersecurity (DNSC). More than 6 in 10 Romanians aged 50 and older identify spoofing or bank impersonation as the most common method of fraud During the ING SAFE Talks event, the first national study on online financial fraud among people over 50 was also released. More than 6 in 10 people over the age of 50 say they have experienced at least one type of cyber fraud, while only 37% say they have never faced such a situation. On average, older adults are familiar with 7 of the 13 types of fraud analyzed in the study. According to the study*, Romanians over the age of 50 are familiar, on average, with 7 of the 13 types of fraud analyzed in the national study: 66% of respondents say they have heard of fake messages or calls that appear to come from a bank or other institutions (spoofing and impersonation methods), which is the most widely recognized fraud method analyzed in the study. Phishing – that is, sending suspicious links to fake websites that mimic official platforms—ranks second (63%), followed closely by offers for products or services at unrealistically low prices and messages or emails requesting passwords, personal information, or account updates (61%). More than half of respondents say they have heard of requests for money received via WhatsApp, Facebook, or TikTok (57%), as well as fake investments and unrealistic financial promises (56%). “The results of this study confirm that financial and digital education must become an ongoing process, adapted to the evolving nature of online fraud. Through the ‘Nesupus Fraudelor’ campaign, carried out in partnership with ING Bank Romania, we aim to provide seniors with practical information, concrete examples, and tools to help them recognize fraud attempts and respond appropriately. The study provides us with a clear picture of the challenges faced by people over 50 and will serve as the foundation for the next stages of the campaign.” — Alexandra Dobre, founder of the Romanian Institute for Active Aging According to the study, most people over 50 choose to take action when faced with a fraud attempt. Nearly seven in ten respondents (69%) say they contacted the police or other authorities, and 47% blocked the contact from whom they received the message. At the same time, more than one-third (36%) verified the information before taking action, and one in five (19%) chose to ignore the message. Only 11% of respondents admit to clicking on the link they received, and a similar percentage contacted their bank to verify the information. Online fraud has become a global, well-organized, and highly adaptable industry “We’re no longer talking about isolated hackers, but about organized groups with structures similar to those of companies: call centers, recruitment, and IT developers. Using artificial intelligence, fraudsters create voice and video deepfakes, as well as flawlessly crafted messages. Furthermore, personalization based on public data increases the attack’s credibility. The emotions most frequently exploited are: fear, urgency, trust, and financial gain.” — Alin Becheanu, Head of Fraud Monitoring & Prevention, ING Bank Romania At the ING SAFE Talks event, ING Bank Romania launched the ING SAFE ecosystem, which brings together the bank’s initiatives dedicated to fraud prevention and customer protection, as well as new security features. ING SAFE Call is a new security service designed to protect customers against attempts at financial fraud. When ING Bank’s monitoring systems identify a payment that deviates from the customer’s usual behavior, the customer automatically receives a verification call from the dedicated number 0374647233 (i.e., 037INGSAFE). During the call, ING Bank customers can confirm or reject the transaction: press 9 if they recognize and confirm the payment, or press 1 if they do not recognize the transaction or were tricked into making it. With the new ING SAFE Button feature, customers will be able to block access to their accounts directly from Home’Bank if they suspect fraud. Protecting customers from financial fraud is an ongoing priority for ING Bank Romania. We are constantly investing in both prevention and monitoring technologies, as well as in the development of new features that help customers identify and avoid fraud attempts before they can take effect. With the launch of the ING SAFE ecosystem, we are bringing all these initiatives together into an integrated approach that combines technological innovation, education, and partnerships with the authorities,” said Alin Becheanu, Head of Fraud Monitoring & Prevention at ING Bank Romania. How can we protect ourselves from online fraud? Be wary if you receive alarming messages or emails that try to convince you to take immediate action: “Your reservation will be canceled in 24 hours,” “Your account will be suspended.” Never click on links or open attachments from unknown sources if the message is unexpected or if you suspect something is wrong. Contact the platform’s team through a different communication channel to verify the message’s authenticity. Do not install apps at the request of supposed investment agents that would give them control over your device, whether it’s a cell phone or a computer. Warning: they will then have full access to your bank accounts and personal data and will be able to perform any transaction they wish! If you need help with a transaction, contact your bank Make sure you’re not on a clone site, which looks similar to the official one but uses a different or misspelled domain name (a missing or extra letter can be a clue). Never log in to your online banking app using a link received via text message or email, and don’t click on promoted links. Use only the app installed on your phone, or type the app’s URL into a new web browser window. Be wary of online offers that seem “too good to be true.” If they contain phrases such as “guaranteed-return investments” or “unbeatable returns,” they most likely come from scammers. Never complete a transaction until you’re sure it’s what you want. Carefully read any text messages you receive from your bank and make sure to confirm the transaction you intended to make. To recognize online fraud attempts and avoid falling victim to them, stay informed by checking reliable sources such as the DNSC website and the security section on the ING Bank website. https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4554.text: Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer-SD) says Slovakia is ready to help Hungary if the country faces an energy crisis linked to the possible shutdown of the Paks I nuclear power plant. Writing on social media, Fico warned that low water levels in the Danube could force the plant to suspend operations because the river provides cooling water for its reactors. The Prime Minister said he had discussed the situation with Economy Minister Denisa Saková (Hlas-SD) and the head of Slovenské elektrárne, Branislav Strýček. He stressed that Slovakia's nuclear power plants at Mochovce and Jaslovské Bohunice use a different cooling system and continue operating as planned. Electricity production at Hungary's Paks plant has already been reduced from its usual 2,000 megawatts to around 480 megawatts. Hungarian authorities are now assessing domestic generation capacity, electricity imports and possible measures to manage demand. Source: TASR

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/07/knif.text: The attack took place a few minutes after 11.00 a.m. local time at the vocational school complex No. 4 in Ostrołęka. A 19-year-old student at the school attacked both pupils and teachers and passers-by with a sharp weapon before fleeing the premises.According to initial police reports, seven people were injured and were immediately taken to hospital. Two of them are said to be in a serious condition.As Superintendent Tomasz Żerański, spokesperson for the Ostrołęka municipal police headquarters, told the Moja Ostrołęka news website, the suspect was detained on the nearby municipal beach on the Narew river just 25 minutes after the incident was reported. He was wounded at the time of his arrest and taken to a hospital.The investigation is ongoing, with dozens of officers interviewing witnesses and securing evidence."The pupils who remained at the school are being looked after. Officers from the social prevention and pathology unit, who work with young people on a daily basis, are also on site," Superintendent Tomasz Żerański said.Authorities did not provide any information about the suspected motive, or details about the weapon.
